title: Rabbi Chizkiyah Chukok
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: He is mentioned in Jerusalem Talmud Sanhedrin, chapter 3, end of halakhah 9. Hyman considers it a scribal error; the Jerusalem Talmud reads: “Rabbi Huna, Rabbi Pinchas, Rabbi Chizkiyah Chukok did not go up to the lecture that day; Rabbi Hunah pushed and went in, and found Rabbi Yirmeyah distressed.” Hyman proposes the reading “Rabbi Chizkiyah — [it was] crowded (dachuk, not Chukok) — and they did not go up to the lecture, and Rabbi Huna pushed and went in.” Likewise we find all three in Jerusalem Talmud Kiddushin 1:6 and Bava Metzia, beginning of chapter 4; he is Rabbi Chizkiyah, Rabbi Yirmeyah’s student. Mavo HaYerushalmi conjectures that the scribe erred and wrote Chizkiyah twice, and from the second Chizkiyah the word Chukok was formed.

notes.text: Hyman’s dachuk reconstruction and Mavo HaYerushalmi’s duplicated-Chizkiyah explanation are competing proposals. The source Chukok form remains in the heading and quoted text; no native-letter history or identity merge is claimed. The chapter/halakhah locations are Jerusalem Talmud.

The proposed division into Chizkiyah and “crowded” is Hyman’s correction; Mavo HaYerushalmi offers a different scribal explanation. Neither theory is admitted as a demonstrated identity or printing history.
